title: Grateful Dead Live at Seattle Center Arena on 1973-06-26
source: Teddy edited all original aud shnid "12076" with silence removal, heavy hiss reduction, eq'ing and retracking in late 11/2006.

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture with crisp mix and minimal audience patches, highlighting a soaring Here Comes Sunshine and an inventive Other One jam.
ai_review.review: The board recording is praised for its exceptional fidelity, wide stereo image and strong kick‑drum presence, despite a few splice glitches in the early Bertha. Musically the show is a showcase of late‑summer ’73 energy – tight grooves on Box of Rain and Greatest Story, a fire‑blazing Playin' in the Band, and an especially memorable Here Comes Sunshine and Truckin’ → The Other One sequence.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (4‑5) and detailed praise for both performance and soundboard quality give a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Exceptional fidelity after Brown Eyed Women with a clean, even mix and great stereo; occasional splice/skip in early Bertha and near the end, patched audience is slightly tinny but unobtrusive.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Smooth, groove‑heavy set with strong transitions (China→Rider, Truckin’ into The Other One) and a high‑energy second half that keeps the momentum rolling.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is praised as perfect; he “smokes” on several tunes, turns up loudly on 'They Love Each Other', provides strong harmonies and even uses a solo to retune while Phil covers.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s bass work is highlighted as huge in the mix, especially during The Other One and Playin' in the Band; his “kills it” on PITB and picks up slack when Garcia tunes.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's Rhodes appears dramatically during the jams (big presence on Playin', splattering on He's Gone); briefly buried early but resurfaces with force.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s kick drum has notable “umph”; overall drumming is solid and drives the grooves, with both Bill and Mickey providing a tight rhythmic foundation.
